title: The Tiny Change That Killed 114 People
alt_titles: One Steel Rod Brought Down Two Walkways
Approved by Phone. 114 Dead. The Hyatt Disaster
description:
On July 17, 1981, two walkways fell into the crowded lobby of the Hyatt Regency hotel in Kansas City during a Friday tea dance. 114 people died. It was the deadliest structural collapse in American history at the time. The cause was not an earthquake or a bomb. It was a small change to how two steel rods held the walkways up, and nobody checked it properly.

In this documentary we rebuild the design step by step: the original plan, the change, the one weak connection in a steel beam, and the chain of people who each assumed someone else had done the maths. Then we look at how this one disaster changed engineering rules around the world.
